property_summary: After any call to transferOwnership via onlyOwner, owner must remain unchanged when called by a non-owner; the buggy modifier allows anyone to change it, violating this invariant.
After a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner must remain unchanged; the buggy version allows any caller to change the owner.
After a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner must not change; the buggy modifier lacks the msg.sender check, allowing a non-owner to change it.
After a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner must remain as the original owner; the buggy modifier lacks the check, allowing a non-owner to change it, causing owner to differ.

For any caller and any proposed new owner, a call to transferOwnership by a non-owner must leave owner unchanged; the buggy modifier omits the caller check, allowing a non-owner to change owner to any address.
Only the current owner can change the owner, so after any sequence of calls to transferOwnership by a non-owner, the owner must remain unchanged; the buggy modifier lets any caller change it.
After a call to transferOwnership by a non-owner, the owner must remain unchanged; the buggy modifier lets any caller change it.

After the initial owner attempts to transfer ownership to any new owner, the owner state variable must change to that new owner; the buggy modifier always allows the transfer regardless of the sender, so any sender can successfully change it, violating the assumption that only the initial owner can initiate the transfer.
For any caller address, after a call to transferOwnership, if the caller was not the owner before the call, the owner must not change; the buggy modifier lets any caller change it.

For any admissible input, after a non-owner transfers ownership via transferOwnership, the owner remains unchanged in the reference but changes in the mutant because the onlyOwner modifier no longer enforces msg.sender == owner.
After any sequence of valid calls, the address stored as `owner` can only be changed by the current `owner` calling `transferOwnership`; the mutant allows any caller to change it.
After a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner remains unchanged in the reference but changes in the mutant.
For any caller that is not the current owner, a call to transferOwnership must revert on the reference but succeed on the mutant, changing the owner.

For any two calls to transferOwnership by non-owners, the owner after the first call must equal the owner after the second call in the reference, but the mutant can change it on the first call, so the second call may produce a different owner.
Only the contract owner can successfully call owned() without reverting; the mutant allows any address to call it, so a non-owner call succeeds where it should revert.

The onlyOwner modifier must ensure that only the owner can call owned() so that owned() never reverts when called by non-owner; the buggy version allows any caller, causing owned() to succeed for non-owners.

Any address that is not the current owner must not be able to change the owner via transferOwnership; the buggy modifier allows a non-owner to execute transferOwnership, so a non-owner can change the owner.

After any successful call to transferOwnership, the owner must equal the address passed as the _newOwner argument; the buggy version sets owner to msg.sender instead, violating this when msg.sender differs from _newOwner.
For any owner and any new owner address, after a successful call to transferOwnership, the owner should be updated to the new owner; the buggy version never updates the owner.

After a successful call to transferOwnership from the current owner, the owner address must equal the passed _newOwner; the buggy version never updates owner, so the check fails for any _newOwner different from the current owner.
